title: Leaves for healing (Revelation 22:1–5)
hookLine: a river of life, and a tree whose leaves heal the nations

lines: A TREE IN THE FIRST GARDEN.
A FLAMING SWORD KEEPS THE WAY.
THE SAME TREE, BY A RIVER.
cards: The Bible's first garden has a tree of life in the middle.
The last time Genesis shows that tree, there's a guard in front of it: God placed "Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life."
The garden is left behind, and the story moves on. Now turn to the Bible's last chapter. An angel shows John a river, clear as crystal, running from the throne down the middle of the city's street.
On either side of it stands the tree of life. No cherubim. No sword.

teach.b: First, the river: "a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb."

Ezekiel once saw a river flowing from the temple, deepening as it went, with trees on its banks whose fruit was for food and whose leaf was for medicine. Revelation sets that picture in the holy city.
Second, the tree "bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month." Never out of season; no month when the branches are bare.
Third, the leaves: "and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations." Not one people. The nations.
Earlier in this book, "the nations were angry." Here they're being healed. And healing means there were wounds.

Readers have asked why a city with no more pain still needs leaves for healing. Some hear healing that has already done its work; others, the long mending of old wounds between peoples, still going on in the city's light.
The text doesn't settle it. Fourth, what's gone and what's given: "And there shall be no more curse." Some readers hear the curse after the first garden lifted here.

teach.h: NO MORE CURSE. THEY SEE HIS FACE.
teach.b: Then a line to set beside Moses, who was told no one could see God's face and live: "And they shall see his face." The way to the tree is open again, and the face is no longer hidden.

how: Some Christians read Revelation 22 alongside Genesis 2–3 as the Bible's last garden answering its first, and some churches read 'the healing of the nations' at services of prayer for peace.

games.q: you're John. the angel shows you the tree of life on both sides of the river. what does the text say its leaves are for?
o: for a crown on the Lamb's head.
for the healing of the nations.
games.why: "the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations." not one people: the nations.

practice: Touch a leaf if one's near, a houseplant, a tree, a sprig of herbs, or a leaf in a picture, and notice its veins, its edges, how it feeds a whole plant by taking in light.
Then think of one wound between people you know, two relatives, two neighbors, two sides of a group chat, and without fixing it, hold the leaf and hold them.
If you pray, bring them by name; if not, just breathe with the leaf in your hand.

wordCard.voice: Leaves for healing. The tree of life by the river in Revelation twenty-two, bearing fruit every month, its leaves for the healing of the nations.

orig.note: Greek: healing, care. "for the healing of the nations", Revelation 22:2.
